Chloe / team,

Reviewed Finexa's round 2 redlines and the subprocessor sheet. I captured counsel-level comments and a suggested compromise below — I also annotated the attached PDF (sent back to Julia in a separate email thread). High level: we can accept most of these with measured guardrails. Key items: 

1) Cross-border transfers
- Recommendation: Accept Standard Contractual Clauses (processor-controller variant where appropriate). Include a short transfer addendum referencing SCCs + our technical/organizational safeguards. Add explicit confirmation that transfers for backup/replication are covered.

2) Audit and security rights
- Push back on unlimited on-site audits. Proposed language: "Customer may request evidence of Redwood's security controls (SOC 2 Type II, penetration test summaries, relevant policies). For additional audits, parties will agree scope and cost; on-site audits permitted only for cause with reasonable notice and a mutually agreeable plan."

3) Retention and deletion
- We can accept a 7-year retention cap for regulated payment records, provided Finexa agrees to provide a narrow definition of "payment records" in Schedule X. For operational logs and telemetry we propose a 1-year default with options for export on request.

4) Subprocessors and prior approval
- We cannot practically require case-by-case prior written approvals for all changes. Compromise: 30 days notice for all subprocessor additions + pre-notification and approval for a short list of "Critical Subprocessors" (define as those handling raw customer content or identity/authentication). Provide current Critical Subprocessor list in the schedule.

5) Liability / breach notification timelines
- Confirm Redwood's 72-hour initial notification for suspected breaches; acceptance of commercial reasonable cooperation for investigations. For limits, maintain existing cap language with carveouts where required by law.

6) Data subject requests / deletions
- We will process DSRs per contract; for complex requests requiring export of older records, propose a cost-recovery approach if requests are unusually burdensome.

Evidence & next steps:
- I'll prepare a redline with the language above and propose a short DPA addendum for transfers and critical subprocessors.
- Please confirm whether Finexa will accept DocuSign for signature (we'll route via our legal eSign process).

I'll send the redline PDF shortly. If you want me to soften any of the language for commercial reasons, flag the clauses and I can propose alternate phrasing.

Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
